# Kubernetes Workloads, eBPF Networking & Storage

::: {.callout-note}
**Part 10: Containers & Kubernetes** · Section 10.7  
*Ubuntu 26.04 LTS ("Resolute Raccoon") Reference Platform*
:::

## Executive Summary & Objectives

This chapter establishes the engineering foundations, operational mental models, and production workflows for **Kubernetes Workloads, eBPF Networking & Storage** within modern Ubuntu 26.04 LTS environments.

## Syllabus & Focus Areas

- [ ] **Core & Stateful Workloads:** Pods, Deployments, ReplicaSets, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Jobs/CronJobs, Init/Sidecar containers, Probes (liveness, readiness, startup), Pod Disruption Budgets
- [ ] **Scheduling & Autoscaling:** Resource requests/limits, QoS classes, Taints & Tolerations, Node Affinity, Topology Spread Constraints, HPA, VPA, Karpenter
- [ ] **Cilium (eBPF CNI) & Gateway API:** Replacing `kube-proxy` completely with Cilium eBPF, L3/L4/L7 `NetworkPolicies`, Cilium BGP Control Plane + L2 announcements, Kubernetes Gateway API (`HTTPRoute`, `GRPCRoute`, `TLSRoute`)
- [ ] **Persistent Storage (CSI):** `StorageClasses`, PVCs/PVs, `VolumeSnapshots`, deploying Rook-Ceph, Longhorn, or OpenEBS ZFS LocalPV on Ubuntu nodes
- [ ] **Kubernetes security:** RBAC (`Roles`, `ClusterRoles`, `Bindings`), `ServiceAccounts`, Pod Security Admission (`Baseline` / `Restricted`), Kyverno / OPA Gatekeeper, and runtime detection with Falco or Tetragon; verify component support and deployment-specific requirements

## Architectural Concepts & Mental Model

Understanding the subsystem architecture, system boundary layers, and kernel-userspace interactions:

- **Target Release Context:** Standardized on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS defaults (Linux 7.0 generic kernel, pure `cgroup v2`, `sudo-rs`, OpenSSH 10.2).
- **Core Abstractions:** Subsystem primitives, state machines, and configuration hierarchies.
- **Integration Points:** Interaction with `systemd`, security layers (AppArmor 4.x), and network/storage fabrics.

## Common Traps, Failure Modes & Recovery

| Symptom / Failure Mode | Root Cause | Safe Remediation & Recovery |
|------------------------|------------|-----------------------------|
| Service startup failure / degraded state | Configuration syntax or permission mismatch | Inspect unit status and journal logs (`journalctl -xeu <unit>`) |
| Unintended state mutation | Legacy utility flag discrepancies | Verify command semantics against `rust-coreutils` and `sudo-rs` |
| Latency or resource starvation | Unbounded resource exhaustion | Check cgroup pressure metrics (`/proc/pressure/*`) |
